name: Fundación Ludwig de Cuba
known: Officers are unpaid: president Carole Rosenberg, chairman Bennet Grutman;
Hernández is a director (ProPublica).
The Havana Film Festival New York is financed by the American Friends, not by Cuba's film institute ICAIC, its artistic director Diana Vargas told NECSUS (2023).
The US arm files a public Form 990 listing its directors.

name: Fábrica de Arte Cubano
known: Founded by the musician X Alfonso.

In its 1 January 2026 communiqué FAC said it receives no government money, that it depends on its members and private actors, and that its director and private businesses in the space paid for infrastructure and maintenance (stated by the space, via Periódico Cubano).

name: Gran Teatro de La Habana Alicia Alonso
Instituto Cubano del Arte e Industria Cinematográficos (ICAIC)
Instituto de Artivismo Hannah Arendt (INSTAR)
known: Independent art and civic-education institute at Tejadillo 214, Old Havana, in the home of its founder, the artist Tania Bruguera (14ymedio, 2015;
Counts the 915 backers of its crowdfunding campaign as its founders, and states that it works apart from Cuban state institutions and rejects censorship (INSTAR).
Estudio Bruguera: donations from the founder's studio, which INSTAR says come from her payments for lectures and workshops and sales of her works.
Cuban authorities detained founder Tania Bruguera in December 2014 and January 2015;

name: Muestra Joven ICAIC
known: Film exhibition for young Cuban directors, held in April and sponsored by the Instituto Cubano del Arte e Industria Cinematográficos (ICAIC), according to the Muestra Joven site.
Its board of directors includes filmmakers (OnCuba).

The competition covers fiction, documentary and animation by directors aged 35 or under, with a poster contest and "Haciendo Cine", a lab for low-budget projects that ends in a pitch to bodies that support production.
2018: ICAIC moved one film to a 24-seat room; the director withdrew it. 2020: ICAIC cut a documentary and at least six filmmakers withdrew works.

name: Museo Ernest Hemingway (Finca Vigía)
known: The Finca Vigía Foundation built a conservation centre on the grounds with wet and dry laboratories and a climate-controlled vault, inaugurated at the end of March 2019 (Matador Network, reposted by the foundation).
The US Embassy in Havana also sponsored the foundation's photograph conservation workshops in April and September 2024 (AIC Photographic Materials Group listing).

In June 2015 the foundation's director said the US State and Treasury departments had authorised four containers of construction materials for the workshop; the project went to the US government in October 2014 and was authorised in May 2015 (OnCuba).
The US foundation files a public Form 990 naming its directors and paid staff.
The US State Department and Treasury authorised the foundation's 2015 shipment of four containers for an on-site conservation workshop.

name: Museo Nacional de Artes Decorativas
known: Attached directly to the CNPC, the Ministry of Culture's heritage council, which names its director; its money is state heritage budget under Ley 155.

name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes de La Habana
known: The director is Jorge Fernández Torres.

name: Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de Cuba
Museo de la Ciudad de La Habana
known: In 2024 the Office's deputy director said large companies still hand over their historic-centre profits to the Office; she named none, and her statement concerns the Office as a whole (Diario de Cuba).

name: Oficina del Historiador de la Ciudad de La Habana
known: In an interview with Russia Today reported on 22 July 2024, deputy director Perla Rosales said the Office has at least seven million a year in hard currency for social projects, with housing and school money coming from many countries and from tourism.
